sources.title: Stanford d.school, Design Thinking Bootleg
sources.verified: The introductory toolkit identifies five modes: Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test. Activities can start anywhere; cards may stem from more than one mode.
sources.implication: Label these as five modes rather than a universal linear recipe. Do not count implementation as Stanford's sixth mode.
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; official page explicitly states the license. Preserve authorship and adaptation credit if using a diagram.

sources.title: Carissa Carter, Let's Stop Talking about THE Design Process
sources.verified: Stanford treats the familiar five-mode sequence as an introductory scaffold. Teaching should develop abilities and adapt methods to the challenge, constraints and learning goals.
sources.dateNote: Original article October 2016; current page has a 2025 posting header. Cite Carter (2016) for the original argument.
sources.implication: The opening can state what students should learn to do, not only which artifacts they should produce.

sources.title: Design Council, Framework for Innovation
sources.verified: Double Diamond describes divergent exploration followed by convergence across Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver. Discover examines the problem with affected people; Define focuses the challenge; Develop explores alternative answers; Deliver tests and improves candidate solutions. Iteration can return to earlier activities; prototypes can be used during discovery.
sources.implication: Explain it as another lens, not a relabeling of the five Stanford modes or an implementation lifecycle.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0; official page explicitly states the license.

sources.title: Design Council, The Double Diamond
sources.verified: Official diagram and attribution available from this page; it is a visual representation rather than a prescriptive instruction manual.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0; credit Design Council and indicate modifications if redrawn.

sources.title: ISO 9241-210:2019, Human-centred design for interactive systems
sources.verified: Standard provides requirements and recommendations for human-centred principles and activities throughout the interactive-system lifecycle. Official ISO record confirms the 2019 second edition remained current after its 2025 review.

sources.title: ISO-authored 9241-210:2019 preview, hosted by iTeh
sources.verified: Clauses 5.1–5.5 specify understanding people/tasks/environments, involvement across development, evaluation with users, iteration, the whole UX, and multidisciplinary work. Table 1 names activities: understand context, specify requirements, produce solutions, evaluate against requirements. The standard complements varied development processes; it does not impose one process. Iteration revises requirements and designs as evidence emerges.
sources.implication: A small four-activity cycle is a useful authoritative foundation; paraphrase it as a course synthesis, without reproducing the ISO figure.

sources.title: GOV.UK Service Manual, Learning about users and their needs
sources.verified: Research continues throughout development. Needs should be evidence-based and state a person's problem rather than prescribing a feature. Opinions unsupported by users are assumptions for research.
sources.implication: Show a traceable chain: observation, interpretation, research question, tentative requirement, prototype, evaluation.

sources.title: GOV.UK Service Manual, Making prototypes
sources.verified: Prototype fidelity should fit the question. Sketches support early exploration; realistic interactions may require code. Prototype code does not satisfy production requirements automatically; learning should continue after release.
sources.implication: Distinguish an artifact used to learn from a maintained live service. Passing a prototype test is evidence for a decision, not proof of universal success.

revisionNotes: Recuperate dall’archivio le due pagine dell’apertura precedente, ora nelle tavole 003–004; conservate le copertine e tutte le sei tavole della revisione, ora 005–010.
Cinque modalità Stanford distinte dal ponte didattico verso l’implementazione.
ISO, d.school e Double Diamond presentati come cornici complementari, senza corrispondenza rigida uno a uno.
Caso simulato collega segnale, domanda, prova e decisione.
Obiettivi di apprendimento distinti dagli artefatti prodotti.
Rivisti i testi e i richiami alle fonti in risposta ai commenti 90–97; aggiunti gli asterischi delle note e rimosse le ripetizioni nella definizione della d.school.
Il diagramma Double Diamond conserva l’asset e l’attribuzione originali; scala 0,513825, credito leggibile e riferimento alla sua introduzione nel 2004.
